Restricted mean survival time is a useful way to summarize survival information on a time scale that is directly interpretable.

## Definition

For a survival function `S(t)`, the restricted mean survival time up to horizon `tau` is the area under the survival curve from zero to `tau`.

$$
\mathrm{RMST}(\tau) = \int_0^\tau S(t)\,dt
$$

## Dynamic use

Instead of choosing a single horizon, one can evaluate RMST over several horizons. This gives a dynamic view of how separation between groups evolves over time.

## Interpretation

A difference in RMST between two groups can be read as a difference in expected event-free time up to a fixed horizon. This is often clearer than a hazard ratio when proportional hazards is questionable or when survival curves separate non-uniformly.

## Practical note

When RMST is computed from predicted survival curves, the time grid, interpolation method, and maximum horizon should be stated explicitly.
